title: Derived constant/limit adjunction with its actual projection counit
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] admitting inverse limits of countable towers. Put $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, the category of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system], with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Assume the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal T)$ exist [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and every complex in $\mathcal T$ admits a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal T)}(Z,I)=0$ for every acyclic $Z$. Let $L=\lim:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$ and let $RL$ be its total right derived functor computed by $RL(QI)=Q(LI)$ on such resolutions. Let $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T$ be the constant tower, also denoting its termwise exact derived functor by $\Delta$, and let $e_n:D(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be evaluation. Define $\pi_{n,B}:RL(B)\to e_nB$ on a tower resolution $q:M\to I$ by the inverse-limit projection $LI\to I_n$ followed by $(Qq_n)^{-1}$, with the canonical resolution identifications. The ordinary adjunction $\Delta\dashv L$ induces a canonical adjunction $\Delta:D(\mathcal A)\rightleftarrows D(\mathcal T):RL$ whose counit $\epsilon_B:\Delta RL(B)\to B$ satisfies $e_n(\epsilon_B)=\pi_{n,B}$ under $e_n\Delta=\mathrm{id}$, naturally in $B$ and independently of its resolution. For any category $\mathcal J$, functors $C:\mathcal J\to D(\mathcal A)$, $B:\mathcal J\to D(\mathcal T)$, and natural transformation $\lambda:C\to RL\circ B$, the maps $\eta_j=\epsilon_{B_j}\circ\Delta(\lambda_j)$ form a natural transformation $\Delta C\to B$ in the derived tower category and satisfy $e_n\eta_j=\pi_{n,B_j}\lambda_j$.

proof.text: The constant tower and each evaluation are exact and additive by levelwise limits and colimits. Use their mapDerivedCategory functors and mapDerivedCategoryFactors. The limit functor is additive by preservation of binary products.

proof.text: Upgrade each supplied quasi-isomorphism q:K to I to a monic quasi-isomorphism K to Cone(id_K) direct-sum I, given by the cone inclusion and q. The projection to I is a homotopy equivalence: contract Cone(id_K) using the identity, so the new target is K-injective. This supplies the existing monic K-injective resolution class without strengthening any hypothesis. The supplied natural-transformation bijections exhibit RL with kappa as a right derived functor. The K-injective right derivability structure and invertibility of kappa on its objects show that it remains right derived after postcomposition by the exact derived constant functor. This uses the existing derivability-structure library, whose K-injective lifting argument rests on the K-injective localization Hom bijection.

proof.text: The comparison isomorphism for the exact derived constant functor exhibits it and every postcomposition as left derived. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.derived to the ordinary constant/limit adjunction on cochain complexes. Its derived-epsilon factorization gives Delta(kappa_I) followed by the derived counit equal to the exact-functor factorization followed by Q of the ordinary counit, for every complex I.

proof.text: Compose the exact constant and evaluation factorization isomorphisms; termwise evaluation of constants is definitionally the identity. Lift this isomorphism through Q to define c_n, with exactly the displayed component formula. Define pi_n by c_n inverse followed by evaluation of the derived counit. Naturality of c_n, the counit factorization, and naturality of the evaluation comparison show kappa_I followed by pi_n and the evaluation comparison is Q of the actual limit projection. The final identification is equality of the degreewise ordinary counit with the limit projection, not detection of derived tower maps by evaluation.

proof.text: For any resolution q:M to I, naturality of pi_n transports the projection identity from I to M. Naturality of the evaluation comparison identifies the evaluated Qq; cancel the invertible RL(Qq). For arbitrary J,C,B,lambda form eta by whiskering lambda with the derived constant functor, then composing with the whiskered counit. Naturality of c_n and the definition of pi_n give the component formula. This is a natural transformation in the derived tower category itself.
